article.content_html:
Key Developments

Daytime Emmy Award-winning talk show host and NAACP Image Award winner Sherri Shepherd is preparing to step into the magical role of the Genie in Broadway's hit musical "Aladdin." Her engagement is scheduled to begin on October 16 and conclude on January 3. Shepherd shared her excitement with The Associated Press, stating, "I’ve taken my family, my nieces and nephews, to see this musical and I never dreamed that I would one day be a part of the ‘Aladdin’ family. So I am beyond thrilled."

To prepare for the high-energy, wisecracking character, Shepherd is taking dance and voice lessons, and practicing the signature song "Friend Like Me" during her walks. She views this challenging opportunity as consistent with her career philosophy: "My whole life is, ‘If it scares you, then you say yes.’ And this is no different because it’s completely out of my comfort zone." This will be Shepherd's second appearance on Broadway, her first being the evil Stepmother in "Cinderella" in 2014. She has also performed in several off-Broadway shows. Shepherd, a podcaster and author, is actively seeking advice from Broadway veterans like Kristin Chenoweth, Steven Boyer, and Wayne Brady to hone her performance.

Key Takeaways

  • Sherri Shepherd will join the Broadway production of "Aladdin" as the Genie, with performances scheduled from October 16 to January 3.
  • Shepherd is undergoing rigorous dance and voice training to prepare for the demanding, high-energy role, which she describes as "completely out of her comfort zone."
  • This marks Shepherd's second Broadway role, and she aims to inspire young audiences, much like she was inspired by Stephanie Mills in "The Wiz."

Why It Matters

Sherri Shepherd's casting as the Genie brings a recognizable and beloved personality to one of Broadway's most popular family-friendly musicals. Her enthusiasm for the role and her stated desire to inspire children to "see the possibilities" resonate with "Aladdin"'s status as a gateway show for young theatergoers. The role of the Genie is significant, having earned James Monroe Iglehart a Tony Award in 2014, underscoring the character's impact and the high expectations for Shepherd's performance. Her journey into this challenging role also highlights her commitment to stepping outside her comfort zone and embracing new artistic endeavors.
